I'm a 40k fan, and twin sticks are usually a good time sink for me but the camera in this really spoiled it. There are a couple of camera bugs that I encountered but nothing else in my "38 minutes" of play according to Steam.
Graphics aren't really any trouble for me, they're not terrible but for a 2014 release they are a little poorer than you'd expect.
The camera moves around you in 3D following a preset track, resulting in you having a low side on perspective in some areas that isn't very well suited for the areas I experienced it, or anything up to a high above but not actually top down perspective. As you move it moves, resulting in not being able to really become comfortable with the controls and aiming. It can result in larger groups of enemies that are off camera yet visible on your radar being very hard to hit because it turns out there are environment models in the way or you being unable to guage the correct angle for your shots.
A steady camera at a fixed angle, not even directly top down, would fix everything I've felt is a problem so far and make me willing to retry the game.
For now, I'd recommend only getting this in a bundle or if you're really wanting to own all the 40k titles, it's not worth purchasing on it's own.

**Edited to add a bit more depth to this review**
This is an ok game. It's not something you'll find yourself playing for hours on end, engrossed in the game, but it's allright.
It has some nice art assets and I love the sound design and music. It gives you a very relaxed vibe. I like the forethought in how the teleporting doors operate. When two doors are placed in such a way that it could cause an infinite loop of the ball just teleporting between the two, the ball will instead exit at an angle, preventing this from happening.  I also really like the concept of the game: building the town and rescuing its residents.
But then, I also have some issues with that mechanic. In every game I've played over all these years, when you upgrade a shop you get more things to purchase from that shop. Not here. Instead you get points added to your Kingdom Score. Get a high enough score and you'll get a chest that might have better gear in it, or something else to purchase in the shop. However, the first time I saved my money to upgrade the shop to get a better weapon to help clear the levels and saw that it didn't do anything, I had that "Oh. How disappointing" feeling. Not a big issue, just not what I expected naturally.
The biggest issue I have is how often the ball will hit inside the paddle instead of on its surface, and be deflected down instead of back up like it should. There are also levels where I'm getting 25fps or less. Neither of these things should be happening.
The "Cloud Bound" area is a good example of why I can only say it's an ok game. It's a 3 stage level. Things are fine for the first two levels but then fall apart on the third. This is where the low frame rate starts. I've also had the ball hit a fly without registering the hit, and had it stuck in an endless bounce between the top left tree and top left corner.
Then there's the center area. You end up with a U shape made of unbreakable blocks with 5 Nightmare Stones that you'll need to complete the level. What will happen when you try to get them is that the ball will bounce off one tip of the U, over the gap, bounce off the second tip and never touch the stones inside. I can clear the first two levels in less time than it takes to get those 5 stones. And don't you dare drop the ball either. Even if you completely clear the first two levels of everything, if you drop the ball once, your score gets penalized so severly that it's impossible to get the necessary score for two Dreamstones. And remember how the ball will bounce down sometimes ...... yeah. Makes the entire run feel like a waste of time.
So overall, I like the game well enough and think I'll eventually complete it despite the things I experienced, which could be patched out. It's also impressive what was done with such a small team. Also appreciate that the developer cared enough to read my original (much shorter) opinion. I'll certainly be looking at what comes next from him.

Elder Scrolls IV: Oblivion is one of those games where you can fully immerse yourself within it's environment and society. The world (called Cyrodiil)  has multiple regions of landscape, all giving you a taste of wildlife and roleplaying elements, like old, swampy caves or a great fort in the uplands of Colovia. Everywhere you go you can interact with the environment, from plants and mushrooms to animals and NPCs.
When you open the grate out of the sewer for the first time you realise the immense beauty of lake rumare, but thats the tip of the iceberg. You could if you wish, follow the main quest, and complete it how the developers thought it would be like. Or you can find your own path venture into an unknown cave, or explore the Imperial City's marketplace and see what it has to offer.
The game has oppertunities to be each class as you will, and a race to go along with it. You could be a High Elf Mage, the Arch-Mage of the Arcane University, or a Nordic Warrior, leader of the Fighters guild. There is a great range of quests to complete and level up your character. You may want to find certain items and loot dungeons to find them, while selling what else you find.
The Shivering Isle DLC, lets Sheogorath the Daedric Prince of Madness invite you to his realm, where everything is run a whole lot differently. The Knights of Nine DLC sends you on an epic quest, to defeat Umaril, who threatens Cyrodiil, while worshipping the Nine Divines. Depending on which pack you brought, one edition will come with four DLC houses, each with their own quest, and some other miscellaneous DLC.
So go explore Cyrodiil in all its glory. Be a Warrior, or a Thief, or a Mage or even all of them together! Thats the thing with Oblivion, its an inviting world at your fingertips that will never get old.

Unfortunately what I played was not what I hoped for. The most important part for me, the thing that made this game so cool, the combat, wasn't good. There's a jump kick, a regular kick, and a sweep kick. Thats it without weapons. With weapons you only have the ability to flail your arm wildly or try throwing it. I'm sure at some point this game will become something very special, but thats not right now. I've requested a refund from the steam store and hopfully will be able to buy the finished version of this game some day.

I seriously do not understand the "Mostly Negative" claim on reviews, especially for recent reviews. This game brings so many things together that other games have tried and failed to do. A climbing system that I enjoy, a in-depth crafting system (Basic when it comes to crafting, but there is a LOT to craft. Plenty of cosmetics to decorate houses and buildings.) A building system, while not as good as something like Medieval Engineers it's still a decent system. The leveling is decent, picking recipes to learn each level with points you're given and skill points you can use to enhance your aim for better ranged weapons, strength for melee, encumberance, stamina, health, etc. The NPC's can be a bit laggy, and the thralls sometimes swing way too fast for it to be balanced but I haven't had this much fun on a survival game in a long time. No other game quite puts these things together like this game has, I've played 30+ hours over the course of 4 days.
The game is on a whole other level with friends. Building villages, exploring, discovering cool landmarks and getting an understanding of the map. Hell, even making trade deals with other clans (Silk for steelfire, aloe for iron, plenty of things people need from different areas). Giving your friends roles to help out the clan with their skill points when they level, a dedicated crafter, a warrior, an archer, even a runner who is specc'd into mostly stamina and encumberance to bring resources long distances.
This game is more than I expected it to be, the reviews kept me from buying it since it's release but with the latest expansion that is COMPLETELY FREE, I cannot recommend it more if you have friends to play it with, especially while it's on sale for only 20 bucks.

Warframe made me NOT pre-order Destiny 2, Shadows of War and made me remove Mass Effect Andromeda from my wishlist. Warframe made me even stop playing Diablo 3. Yes, this is a heck of a game! It's a fast-paced, smooth and responsive third person action combat/shooter. The progression system feels rewarding even though it's a free-to-play game. There are microtransactions, but read it carefully: this isn't a pay-to-win game. It feels more like a pay-if-you-want-to-save-time kind of game. The grind exists, sure! This is a looter game after all, but it is so fun that you won't even care after you start to progress. Actually, you don't even need to spend a dime on this game to get access to all the Warframes (the "classes"), weapons, archwings and arch-weapons and companions. Everything is farmable, aside from some skins and community made skins (but they are all cosmetics).
Note that this is a 2013 game, but the developers are still strong in updating this game up to this day. It had changed a lot and most of the major changes, aside from more content, they were made to the graphics, mechanics, economy, playability and usability. This is the kind of free-to-play game that you won't believe it was free once you start playing. Actually, the prejudice of free-to-play games is the only thing stopping this game to be one of the most succesful games ever created in this "new generation".
From the actual gameplay perspective, you will feel like you are playing something like Mass Effect, but as a space ninja, because you can sprint, jump, double jump, bullet jump, latch into walls, walk into walls, climb walls, aim and shoot in any direction while you are moving, change the aim perspective (left and right), you can melee attack with A LOT of variety of melee weapons (swords, scythes, hammers, daggers, whips, staffs, dual-whatever, etc) and all Warframes (the "classes") have 4 different abilities and 1 passive. You can play as a tank, melee dps, support, healer, stealth, sniper... you choose. There is a lot of things you can do that it's difficult to tell them all in a simple review.
Well, in all, if you like Destiny, Mass Effect and looter games like Diablo and Borderlands, believe me, you WON'T regreat it. Download it now, make an account and be prepared to be amazed.

In order to understand why I like this game so much, bear with me for a second while I share a small story. Ivan the 2nd was the new ruler of Muscovy. His father had expanded the duchy greatly, but he had 3 sons. Ivan was the eldest, and his two younger brothers were not even of age yet. Still, when Dad suddenly died they each received a bit of the massive duchy.
Ivan the 2nd was not happy about this state of affairs. Ivan had weak claims on each of their kingdoms, but he couldn't press them via war. The middle brother was just a few months away from turning 16 and he could get a wife! If he got a wife then that meant children and Ivan the 2nd would never get that territory back from his brothers.
Then a terrible, awful, evil idea entered his mind. If he couldn't fight them directly, there was another way to inherit the provinces. After all, if something were to suddenly "happen" to his two younger brothers, then he stood to get everything. What a tragedy it was when both of the young children suddenly died in mysterious circumstances before they could have children of their own. Then Ivan the 2nd formed the Kingdom of Rus just in time for the Mongols to show up. Oops.

I've put a little bit of time into this, so I guess I might as well write something.
A solid co-op shooter that goes out of its way to make you feel like a whirling, flying death machine. You have tons of options in how you want to mow through hordes of enemy space marines, robots, and space zombies. The different warframes are fun and unique, each bringing their own power set to the mix. You got stuff like a dragon-knight that only gets stronger when he gets hurt, or a bard that plays (literal) killer tunes, or a guy that can literally be built to be One-Punch Man.
You got weapons that range from the standard guns and melee to the crazy. Wanna use the Spartan Laser from Halo? We got that. Wanna use a shotgun that fires massive shards of glass? Got it. Wanna use a laser gun that also spews floating land mines? Sure, why not. Wanna use a gun that literally just throws massive sawblades that decapitate everything? Say no more. Wanna use a gun that is literally just a weaponized fart? I dunno why you'd ask for that, but hey, we got it.
The fashion game is strong here. Right off the bat you can fully recolor everything you get, swap out helmets, add armor pieces, get sick scarves and more. In the end, the mantra always applies: "Fashionframe is the true endgame."
The F2P model is one of the more fair ones out there right now. Every single weapon, warframe, and companion is obtainable for free, and it's not a huge hassle to do so (mostly, there are a couple outliers but they are by far the exception and not the rule). This game also does something that you don't see very often: you can trade the premium currency, so even the stuff that would normally be cash-only in most other F2P games are totally earnable through regular gameplay here.
The devs clearly care a lot about this game, it's basically their baby, and they had to fight to make it what it is (look up the history of the game Dark Sector if you got a minute and wanna see where this game's origins are). They make weird decisions sometimes but they listen to and work with the community to make it work.
TL;DR: its okay i guess

Kill Team is a twin stick shooter set in the 40k universe where you play a space marine kill team trying to take down an ork crusier.  There is very little in the way of story beyond this.  you will be told to go somewhere and blow somthing up or kill somthing until you fight the warbosses at the end and thats it.
The game is basic as hell. you pick one of four classes and mow or chop down dozens of orks and eventually tyranids.  Occasionally you pick up power ups or spam a charge attack special move to help with the hairier situations and thats about it.  Its mostly move from point A, killing everything on the way to point B, where you will fight several waves of enemies or one of three bosses.  The enemies boil down to either melee or ranged mobs with varing degrees of health and none of them feel unique from one another.
the two melee and two ranged classes barely feel different from one another save for their special move and you don't really level up. rather getting points unlocks passive buffs and eventaully more powerful main weapons for each class. No skill tree or unlockable special moves.  You can pick from several space marine chapters but all this does is change your color scheme.
The game is really short too. only about 6 or 7 missions that will take you about 30 mins each to beat.  There are unlockable surivial modes but with only a hand full of perks and weapons to unlock why bother?
On top of all this the game is kind of buggy.  During the opening cutscene ugly green pixilated spots appear all over the screen.  i've had the game crash a couple of times losing my progress in a mission and while you can aim in the general direction of the enemies the game automatically aims up or down when your on uneven ground or if your being rushed by small enemies...or at least its suppose to but in practice i usally ended up shooting over or under the enemies and taking hits.  This is espcially noticeable with the the sternguard veterans missle launcher which has a slow rate of fire so every miss is a big deal when your swarmed.  And the game can be really cheap as eneimes can eat your health in seconds (especially the terrorguants), checkpoints are spread too far and the camera is fixed and will somtimes suddenly shift in the middle of battle or even get stuck in places.
This is a boring and at times frustrating slog of a game.  You might get a little fun out of it if you play with a friend but there are way better twin stick games and certianly better 40k games out there.  I'd say skip this game even if its on sale.

I typically do not write a review for a game until I've played it for quite a few hours. I may have only played this one for two hours, but I believe I've found everything the game has to offer. And truthfully, I wanted to enjoy it... but I felt I was lost in a story that made little sense and wasn't captivating.
There are also the following core issues:
- The fancy handwritten script can be extremely hard to read.
- There's no option for subtitles. I usually play with audio anyway, but I always dislike it when games /force/ me to have the sound on.
- There's also no music. Music adds so much to a game, or in this case, NOT having it actually takes away from the experience.
The achievements were also mostly based on repetition; the game had to be completed twenty or thirty times to get everything, and even then, there was little to no guidance on how to get the achievements, so it was mostly me stumbling around blindly clicking on things and hoping an achievement unlocks.
There are some high points, like the voice acting -- it's not great, or even good, but I've also heard much worse. The concept is also cool, though the storyline could have been fleshed out more. It doesn't even do it justice to storylines to SAY this game has a storyline, as it's mostly random tidbits of information about items in a fictional shop coupled with a minorly interesting, not-that-compelling dialogue between The Customer and his Mother-in-Law. Overall, I don't think I can really recommend this game, but if you insist on buying it, I recommend checking out the achievement guide I wrote in the guides section, mostly because it will limit the amount of frustrating repetition that is to be found in this game.

Having gone through the Groundhog Day like loop that is The Shopkeeper over a dozen times at this point, I'm still struggling to make anything of it.
It's built on ambiguity, giving you only the smallest hints as to context and character motives, as it shifts perspectives at a rapid pace to the extent I'm at a loss to say what is or isn't fiction. And that's interesting and thought provoking, but The Shopkeeper doesn't give you enough to work with to be able to derive any meaning out of its characters or handful of repetitive lines of dialog. As a game stuck on repeat at some point you would assume having seen the sames scenes play out so many times you might eventually grasp what the greater purpose, if there is any, of all this must be. But I never found that moment of clarity, as I continuously attempted to cross dialogue paths while arriving at the same non explanatory ending (for lack of a better term) ad nauseam.
There's something fascinating to me about The Shopkeeper, as if something is hiding just behind the curtain and I've merely failed to procure how exactly to pull it away, but for as far as I can tell these lofty ideas are little more than figments of my imagination conjured up to fill the vast emptiness of the experience. Whether or not my hypothesizing is accurate to any degree I have no way of knowing, but if not, they've concealed the greater explanations and revelations so effectively as they may as well not exist at all.

Larian Studios strike again with massive cRPG game and if you love this genre - you have to play this one. It's pure game as it gets, no micro-transaction bullcrap, no day 1 dlc, nothing - just a brilliant game made with passion.
Obviously the game is not perfect, no game is and nothing is, but it's bloody good. You start the game you are not hand-held by anything, you figure you way thru and do your things your own way. You have plenty of option to choose from, starting from your own character - you have many playstyles to choose from: fighter, summoner, necromancer, archer, rogue assassin, mage of 4 different forces of nature, polymorphy and you combine those anyway you like to make a truly unique build and experience in gameplay. You can create your own character from scratch or play one of the 6 origin characters. The origin characters serve as fantastic companions to choose from as well, all of them being different and unique in personality and special abilities. All companions have a unique storyline to experience.
The quests, dialogue writing and exploration feel really good and thru your gameplay you'll be accompanied with brilliant music written this time by a new composer (Borislav Slavov) and it's up to par with original composer that worked for Larian for so many years, but sadly passed away soon after prequel of this game came out (rest in piece Kirill Pokrovsky). Unlike many other cRPG - this one is fully voice acted for all NPC and a narrator and it ads to immersion - believe me!
Combat is one of the best in cRPG games in my honest opinion. It's tactical turn-based combat, but it's not hexagon map based. Instead you only have range units that limit you how far you can move your character or how far you can reach with your skills and how big area you can cover - this way it feels more natural. Each turn your party characters get set amount of action points and there your tactics begin on how to use them - whether to strike some damage, crowd control enemies, buff you or your party member, or move your character to a new position. On top of that - you can combo elements for extra effects: fire + oil = massive explosions, etc. You can use environment to your advantage or it can be used by the enemy against you - so play smart, every decision matters and has consequences. You cannot ask for a better combat in cRPG.
Ofc there are few minor problems with the game - a minor bug here and there, but nothing impacting your experience a lot and story is not the best I've seen in genre, but it's solid enough to suck you in.
I didn't play 10/10 game yet (because it would have to be absolutely perfect in every way - that's how strict I am) but Divinity Original Sin 2 is close one. My 9/10 would be 10 for most reviewers out here.
If you are looking for fantastic adventure without being held by your hand - the game is for you. If your are looking for modern cRPG - Divinity Original Sin 2 should be your prime choice!

Divinity 2... To start simply, if you liked the first Divinity: Original Sin title, you'll absolutely love this. As far as I'm concerned this just takes the first game, improves on near every aspect if not all of them, and gives you a genuinely great experience.
As I type this, I have 35 hours and between making new saves to play with friends, and making new saves to try new classes, I haven't even touched act 2. The classes are all so fun but also very open, you can tweek them to play exactly as you want them to which opens some interesting avenues. Want to play a front line tank that can heal, essentially a paladin? Go for it! Want to play a stealthy rogue that has the capability of debuffing enemies while swooping in and out of the fight? Sure, do it, nothings stopping you.
The game being so open is what's kept me repeating the same early game multiple times, and it doesn't get old. The characters are all great, voice acting is generally brilliant and I've found myself walking around town talking to everyone not in hope of progressing the plot or discovering a new quest, but because I find the characters interesting.
The multiplayer is, ofcourse great. Any game like this where you can also play with up to 3 friends is only improved by that co-operative aspect, be it genuinely trying to fight and progress, destroying eachother in the arena, or simply messing around teleporting eachother and being general♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ it's just a fun experience made better with your buddies adventuring by your side.
Due to my lack of progression I can't talk much for the late game, but after these hours sunk into just the first act, I can promise you you'll get your monies worth.
Divinity: Original Sin 2 is one of the only newly launched games that I have found a genuine appreciation for. I find there's a lack of heart put into video games nowadays, all just hunting for that sweet sweet money. But with Divinity 2, there's clearly been time, effort, and care pumped into this game, making it the brilliant experience it's shaped to be.

Overfall, a comical turn-based roguelike game.
One of the few greats out there for those who enjoy deep tactical turn-based games with fantasy on the side.
After finishing the game twice after having unlocked most of the content available, I am satisfied. Might return one day when I'm bored even! - Because it has impressive depth for a game which at first could give a bland impression.
The gameplay is easy to learn, hard to master, at first sight one might think it's simplistic. But that is far from the truth, its like saying a shooter game is very simple, and ignoring all the tactical depths those usually have - movement, sound etc. - Here it is personas, debuffs and buffs which will save or kill your party. You can have 4 at most, 2 characters which you start out with and 2 companions you will find on your adventures. The amount of optional characters and companions is impressive.. very much so even.
The most positive thing about it is the amount of optional companions, items and characters you can unlock, hunting them throughout the islands might be a chore for some, but for me it felt satisfying to gain new optional playstyles. No companion is bad, none op either. But if you read their skills and abilities carefully, there are very powerful combinations in battles you can unlock if you pick the right party.
The adventures on the islands are short, but entertaining, sometimes downright hilarious, it all depends on your sense of humor. Sometimes even when you try to be the absolute saviour of the world.. your good actions might actually turn really foul, so much that it's funny.
The choices you can make in them is limited to -two ways- usually, which is a bit limited in my opinion.
Pros:
Deep tactics are possible with huge amounts of options for your party, more options than you can possible explore before you've finished the game.
Many different adventures on the islands
Art, if you like it - I do!
Music, if you like it - I do!
Lastly, the story is quite interesting if you care about those things.
Cons:
A bit too few adventures, not enough endgame for a player to have time to try out all kinds of characters and/or companions before the endgame feels repetitive. Yes I've said there are many of them, this is true. But it is barely enough to contain a guy who wants to experiment before it is finished. Hunting enemies only for the battles isn't enough for me.
I don't understand why it isn't possible to upgrade the companions as you can do the Characters you start with - even if they are Perma-dead when they die in this game, it would have been a fun thing to do.
Summary: In the end, I warmly recommend this jewel. Would've loved to be part of a team making a game like this.

Awesomenauts is a free-to-play very fun, fast, light, easy to pick up MOBA type (ex: dota2 or league of legends) game.  This game is 3v3 player vs. player, and plays similar to smash brothers, as a fighter/ light platformer, but the game mode is MOBA style with both teams trying to push waves of minions towards the enemy base, with turrets along the way.
The character roster is good sized and includes a variety of playstyles like long range nuker, quick stealthy sneak attacker, crowd control focused tank, and so on.  The difference in playstyle keeps the game feeling fresh if you want to try new nauts, but perfecting a single character will keep you playing too.
I find that in contrast to other popular MOBA games, I almost never rage in this game.  The game is so light weight and fun feeling that even a loss still can feel fun.  Each match lasts about 15 minutes or so, so you can find yourself experiencing lots of games in a session of gaming which is nice too.

Awesome game!! It exceeded my expectations at all levels save one; the graphics performance is underwhelming. It's running at sub 60fps, not at minimum settings but even at minimum doesn't seem improve the frame rate. OK aside from performance issues, i have not encountered big bugs except in the initial stages after i had done a lot of tweakings. It randomly crashed twice while i was driving. Maybe it was due to too many changes and clicking the apply button. All is well now but with a slightly low performance as mentioned before.
So what's so good about this game? Well it's more than a truck♥♥♥♥♥business sim; it's also has a story.
Lets go over the features.
1) As a truck sim there are;
a) Headlights
b) Signal lights
c) Wipers
d) Parking brake
e) Engine brake
f) Truck equipment / component upgrades
g) repairs & maintenance costs
h) fuel requirement
i) hazard lights
j) horn
k) and of course, buying more trucks and upgrading your own truck (like in Hard Truck 2)
2) As a business sim there are;
a) Hire & fire drivers
b) buying more trucks
c) monitoring schedules
d) managing cash flow
e) expanding business reach by adding offices in other towns
f) competing with other companies (like in Hard Truck 2)
3) As a story;
a) a personal log of encounters along the way
b) cutscenes of your journey aka story
c) detailed animated characters
d) excellent voice acting
So what about the environment? Well it's good enough at low settings so it should be pretty impressive if maxed out. The road curves and hills are smooth, no jarring crude polygons as it once were in Hard Truck 2. No road mines either so that's a relief! Day and night cycles and weather cycles. The roads and highways, they are expansive and very impressive, at least to me. While driving from town to town there's plenty to see of the environment though some might disagree.
And driving physics? Seems very good, you can see the motion of the suspension on the individual wheels. Keyboard sensitivity can be adjusted from fast to slow. So does the centering rate. These 2 settings are very useful in finding the right balance to suit individual driving preference.
What about graphics and sound quality? All great! Trucks look detailed both in and out. Reflection details and rate of update can be adjusted many levels. Shadow details and viewing distance can also be adjusted many levels. Same with HDR and truck detail levels. In short all adjustable settings are graduated from 1 to 10 steps. Some settings only have on or off. It should be quite easy to find the right balance of quality and performance for any machine that meets the system requirements. Engine whirr and growl sounds real IMO. Radio stations play a wide selection of quality music. You can even add your own station like in Test Drive Unlimited.  Radio is one aspect where Rig 'n' Roll shine. You can hear up to 3 people talking in between music at random and they are rather funny & witty. What is even more amazing is the fact that the talking voices even interrupts your radio station.
Final aspect, nearly neglected to mention is the brilliant AI which ties the whole game together and is nothing short of amazing. Where in most other driving or racing games, the traffic or NPC AI is either dumb or gets in the way or pops in & out of existence at random just to block your path; in this game that rarely happens, even when you're racing with other AI truckers. AI traffic & other AI truckers not participating in the same cargo run, would never get in your way unless overtaking another AI traffic which is in-front of them. Even when your're driving against the flow, the AI traffic & other AI trucks cleverly avoid head-on collision. AI seems to extend even to the radio interruptions. For example; they might talk about the need to upgrade engine when your diving rather slowly in a race. The talking voices isn't there just to lend a live effect to the stations they also talk about random events that are happening in the game. Some messages given by the radio appears in your journal as clickable entries which may include random quests. Therefore turning on the radio becomes a necessity if you want to participate in the random events.
Cops are very aggressive and tenacious. It's almost impossible to lose them. If you go to a warehouse, they will follow you in or be waiting outside and continue the chase when you leave. If you refuse to stop, more cops will chase you and try to run you off the road. The resulting fines and damages to your rig can negate all rewards for the delivery or race run. So it's usually best to stop & pay-up at the first sign of a siren. Though it's possible to lose them, should they catch you later the previous fines are added to the current one. Also any accidents involving AI vehicles is deemed your fault no matter what; the cops are on a mission to give you a hard time. Never cross a yellow line in front of a cop or they will chase you to hell and back! Despite all the problems the cops can dish out, there's a neat feature called save game which can be made at any time while driving so you can immediately undo that horrible crash or wong turn you just made. ;)
Game world is huge, beautiful and detailed. The lighting and reflection effects on the road when it drizzles and vehicle surfaces are impressive. It's best to look around while driving to appreciate the game world but accurate and dexterous finger work is a must to avoid crashing into objects while not looking where you are going and controlling the camera views simultaneously. This game is a big improvement over Hard Truck 2 in all aspects. Glad i bought it despite the 'Mostly Negative' rating at the time of this writing.
Lastly you don't need a wheel to drive well in this game; it works just fine with a keyboard. But you'll need a high-end rig to get the most out of it. Don't miss this underrated gem; try it for yourself. I absolutely love it! 4/5 stars.

'It's like real trucking, only not really." 5/10
This game gave me a ton of respect for truckers. Before I played it, I thought they just drove from one warehouse to the other lining their pockets with cash. But once I found out that every time they bump into something, drive slightly off the road, or go ten miles over the speed limit they have cops trying to run them down to arrest them, that changed everything. I know this game is supposed to be a simulator, and I'm sure from time to time truckers do get arrested, especially coming back from Mexico, but did they really have to put that aspect into the game?
I've played a few trucking simulators before and none of them had me getting ripped out of my cab, thrown to the hood of a car, and arrested for "assaulting a police officer". Seriously, I got arrested for that. When the heck did I assault a police officer? I haven't even gotten out of my truck! And why the heck does it always look like it's raining on my windshield, even when it isn't? Ugh. Okay, fine, whatever, that doesn't sound SO bad, right? Okay, but since when do truckers have to compete with one another to get their load to the warehouse first so they can get paid? Yep, this game makes delivering cargo into a race to the finish line with three other hungry truckers. Oh, you want money for food and other living expenses? Better get here first! What the heck is this, the Hunger Games? But what else did I expect from a 1C Racing game? I should have known better.
Aside from the ridiculousness though, this game has some decent views, not such awful graphics, and once you get it configured with a controller (which is a massive pain in the butt), it isn't a complete mess. But don't get me wrong, this game should be avoided. Stay far, far away from this game. And if you actually want a good trucking simulator, pick up a copy of Euro Truck Simulator 2, that game is amazing. Unless you wanna pretend that in this game you're smuggling around a truckload of drugs to make it more believable. But who wants to use their imagination? We bought the game specifically so that we didn't have to do that!

I honestly feel like I am in an abusive relationship with this game. On one hand, the story is fantastic, the characters and set pieces are absolutely amazing, and the combat is really rewarding.
My biggest gripe with the game is the difficulty of some of the encounters. The game is very hard, and for the most part you will just barely survive many of the encounters. I think this is fine, as it gives you a sense of achievement. But then there are a handful of important encounters in the game, that are just absolutely merciless. If you just run into these with your party in the standard formation for the first time, you will most likely have most of your team dead and the rest with very low health before you even get the chance the act. Other times, the combat drags on when there are a lot of enemies and just when you think you are winning, something unexpected happens and you die. This can be really frustrating when you have been fighting for 10+ minutes and just barely managed to turn the tide in your favor.
The quests can also feel a bit loose sometimes with npc's having to be reminded that you have met, and that they have given you a quest. The quest log can also be very unhelpful at times since it does not order information chronologically according to the quest, but instead as the information is found by the player.
Overall would I recommend it? Absolutely. But if you are a casual player I would definitely recommend starting the game on explorer mode.

UPDATED with tips
To clear up some out of date or just plain wrong information in some of the other reviews.
-The game DOES play in Widescreen
-Co-op mode is Local on the same machine, the second player needs a controller (you can use keyboard and mouse)
-If you are playing solo on keyboard and getting controller tips UNPLUG YOUR CONTROLLER
-Having played this game thoroughly (over 10 hours and 11/12 achievements at time of writing) the only bug I found was blocky green artifacts in the video intro
-The game is 2011 vintage, not truly 2014, as it's a console port
Tips for the campaign
-The easiest class to solo with is the Sternguard Veteran followed by the Tech Marine
-The Tech Marine is probably a better choice for the tricky Tyrannid level, otherwise stick with the Sternguard Veteran
-Powerups don't expire if you don't pick them up, so time picking them up wisely
-Sprint is not infinite, so wait a couple of second before doing it again for full benefit (also cease attacking to move faster, whether sprinting or not)
-Bonuses are down to personal preference mostly, but bonus Ranged damage is almost always useful
Tips for the survival mode Gold Aquila achievement
-You need to survive about 3 and a half minutes
-Try to save the Health Powerups until you really need them
-Generally Ranged bonus damage + a special move modifier is best
-Probably don't attempt the survival mode until you have unlocked +25% bonuses (easily done by mowing thru earlier campaign levels a few times)
-It's worth practicing all the classes on a Campaign level first, so you know their strengths, because you don't get a choice with Survival
-Enemies with ranged weapons should be a priority, as these are the ones that tend to cause the most grief

This game is quite wonderful if you didn't play fallout new vegas before it, many people who don't like Fallen Earth claim thats their reasoning, and I can agree, when I first played Fallout: New Vegas, I drew many comparrisons towards Fallen Earth, and its entirely based on their core gameplay styles, rather than mechanics. But this game is more balanced towards PvE, unlike fallout, you actually have true crafting and scavenging that doesn't just give you what your looking for, you have to make it, or learn it, unless you have friends in high places, such is the true life of a survivor in an apocolypse. This game also offers a nice explaination for one of gamings biggest mysteries, respawning. You have a collar, which transfers your DNA into a chamber, reconstructs you atom by atom, and gives you a "new life" as a clone of yourself, something I wish was in other games rather than "you died, restart" the game is vastley large, I could easily see Skyrim's map fitting within all the sectors, possibly more than once, and weapons are vast in the beginning, as you get stronger, weapons tend to become more scarce, with good reason, so you rely much more on your skills than an overpowered Bumper Sword, and with the character menus, such as Abilities and Stats, your options are endless in what type of character, or "toon" you'd like to create, vs. Bethesda's way of "upgrade it all over time" your more limited, but in a good way, and you have the ability to reset all your stats and start over to specifically fit how you play, along with the adition of mounts, which start off bad, give you 7 types of vehicles to choose from, Horse, ATV, Motorcycle, Dune Buggy, Chopper, Station wagon, and Sports car, they also have different types of each, an example would be "dune buggy" vs. "cargo buggy" or "chopper" vs. "Tribal Chopper" they have different stats, and each vehicle handles certain terrain better than others, as well as the ability to have more than one vehicle. The crafting is intuitive and very thourough, with real time crafting that takes time to make more complex items so you can't just spit out the best of something like a machinegun with the right tradeskill componants, it gives you a greater sense of acomplishment by knowing you built something that took hours rather than buying it from the Auction House, though as I said before, with friends in high places, anything is possible, I suggest craft early on as much as you can, ask the Help Channel for any information, for myself and others often know detailed answers on how to complete a task or quest, or locate specific items. The Wiki can be useful too, utilizing tools given to the player and figuring out your best way to play is the greatest part of the journey, to see all the pieces fall together:... IN SHORT: This game is for DEDICATED PLAYERS, those who will take the time to do these things listed, and many more unlisted tasks, some amazing, some time crunching, to acomplish your higher, longterm goals. I recommend this game to those looking for something to pour their hours into and want something that keeps giving them different challanges to overcome, AS FOR THE CASUAL PLAYER, I suggest giving it a try and seeing how you enjoy it, but not taking it to heart that it will be like fallout or anything that simple, its a rough game, for rough players, and if you don't like it, you can simply move on to another game, though I must warn you, I've found few MMORPGs as interesting as this one, only POTCO could hold my attention longer than this, and that may have been because of its simplisity and fun nature towards its gamers. With that being said... Enjoy the Apocolypse.

I really wish Steam reviews have a 'Sorta' option for recommending games.  But since it doesn't, thumbs down is what it has to be.
The world is interesting, graphics are good, sound assets are fine and the music is fine in most places.  I'm enjoying playing the game though there are some things that are making me grit my teeth and groan in frustration:
1. Targeting bug:  Quite often I find I can't target an enemy until I rotate the camera to a certain angle.  This often makes me move when I don't want to, and completing throwing a fight.
2.  The Ai cheats a LOT.  Being able to see through walls with attacks, ignoring elevation rules for LOS, and pixel perfect target selection that is not possible for players to do.
3.  Unfair rights.  My gear is the best I can get (the game is painfully stingy with loot considering the price of items,) and I find some fights utterly unfair even though the enemies are the same level I am.  Some creatures are excessively difficult for their level and the numbers they appear in.  Regularly I'm finding fights end with my main character being the only one alive because attacks do 200-300 in one hit oneshotting half my party and stun locking them.  Often this happens during the surprise round when my party is clumped together, or when  *sigh* SURPRISE re-enforcements arrive.  It is tiresome and unfun.
4. Scaling seems out of wack.  The higher my level the weaker I seem to be.  Enemies become tougher, stronger, faster, etc while the party progresses in a much slower rate, and are often underlevelled for encounters.
The game is almost great, but it desperately needs some balance tweaking to keep me playing for much longer.

Overfall almost passed under my radar due to the underwhelming store page, the screenshots and videos do not do justice to the games true strengths. I think the art style doesn't present well in static screenshots, the style used for the characters in particular looked amateurish and I was worried that Overfall was another cash grab indie title. However, in-game they came to life with nicely drawn animations for all actions, in fact, the deeper into a playthrough I travelled the more diverse the characters became and the better the art style seemed to fit.
Overfall's true strengths are a trifactor of: Gameplay, Replayability & Storytelling and let me say, it has them in spades.
Accolades Overfall can boast are:
Some of the best creative writing I have experienced, awash with many movie/game/media references.
Challenging & strategic hex/turn based combat with emphasis on buffs/debuffs and skill synergies.
A fair risk verus reward rogue-lite with hundreds of random scenarios, encounters and quests.
Many of the scenarios have multiple branches, endings & rewards for maximum replayability
Easy to use yet powerful scenario editor, in which you can make anything from a tiny encounter to a multiple island hopping questline in which the only limitation is your imagination.
Steam Workshop support with loads of player made encounters you can easily add to your game.
In summary, Overfall is a hidden gem of a game which is somewhat let down by its ambiguous name and "amateurish at a glance" art design. It worries me that a significant percentage of gamers may give this game a miss based on these factors, which would be a real shame as Overfall is definately a book you should not judge by its cover.
Score: 9/10 - Highly reccomended.

In order to understand why I like this game so much, bear with me for a second while I share a small story. Ivan the 2nd was the new ruler of Muscovy. His father had expanded the duchy greatly, but he had 3 sons. Ivan was the eldest, and his two younger brothers were not even of age yet. Still, when Dad suddenly died they each received a bit of the massive duchy.
Ivan the 2nd was not happy about this state of affairs. Ivan had weak claims on each of their kingdoms, but he couldn't press them via war. The middle brother was just a few months away from turning 16 and he could get a wife! If he got a wife then that meant children and Ivan the 2nd would never get that territory back from his brothers.
Then a terrible, awful, evil idea entered his mind. If he couldn't fight them directly, there was another way to inherit the provinces. After all, if something were to suddenly "happen" to his two younger brothers, then he stood to get everything. What a tragedy it was when both of the young children suddenly died in mysterious circumstances before they could have children of their own. Then Ivan the 2nd formed the Kingdom of Rus just in time for the Mongols to show up. Oops.

Fantastic game. I highly recommend to anyone that's into FTL and tactical RPGs. I'll try to describe it since it's hard to get a complete picture from the outside:
You have 2 primary party members, gaining up to 2 more, and sail around a series of islands that offer random short choose your own adventure story bits mixed with tactical RPG combat. And it has a larger progression that takes you to a natural endgame. While each of these components isn't super deep they each have enough facets and content to stay fresh replaying it when you fail (it's got a rogue-lite structure).
For example you can unlock new primary classes (available selecting your starting people) new ability sets for them, new secondary classes, and there are multiple variations to the main story of each play through. Different characters give you access to unique choices in the story vignettes too, so while you will start to see repeats it's not unbearable. And there's a good amount of synergies to using classes together that make trying new combinations interesting.

This game is meant for a younger audience it seems and should be reviewed accordingly. Having said that, I am a 28yo female and I still found it quite amusing ^.^ Its a nice change of pace from Darks Souls / Smite etc "serious" games. This game is serious as well. But it's comparatively easier.
- The enemies don't respawn, they have a decent variety and types, some are passive, some are just objects and some are aggressive. They are easy to defeat if you get the timing right. There's sufficient time to correct a mistake but they're not so easy that you can keep whacking the attack and get away with it.
- There are check points which are far enough from where you died to still maintain the platforming challenge but not too far to make it annoying.
- The level design is nice. It has different features and the game overall is quite creatively made.
- The camera is scripted but you can move it and enjoy the game. This game requires patience, and I mean that in a good way. When you arrive on a platform, take your time to judge where things are before leaping. I think its a good lesson for kids (and even some adults)
- Graphics are nice and cute.
- Soundtrack is nice too, this game isn't meant to be played for hours on end consecutively, if you keep your playtime limited to a level, it won't annoy you.

Trying out a more symplistic reviewing style by just mentioning everything what's good and what's bad, titled, "The Good, The Bad and The Verdict". Nice and cliche. Let's go.
Overgrowth is basically a martial arts game with a swing at realism, revolving around a simple story. Both campaigns consist of levels in which the objective is to eliminate your threat, before advancing with the story.
The two things that shine the most are the combat and the environment, as far as graphics go. The combat is most definitely something I haven't seen before and I really like the idea of it being a little different than spamming attack and where you face opponents that, if you don't play your cards right, will destroy you in a single hit. There's a variety of high and low attacks and blocks and you have to look at your enemy and respond to the attack or you'll get hurt.
The environments are also pretty neat. It's set in both nature and a bit of fantasy. There's a forest, swamp, (snowy) plain, village, ship, etc. it all looks good.
Instead of a health bar, the game relies on a skeleton, so to say. Get hit too much in the same place and you'll get knocked out or killed. A sword hit is usually an instant death, rightfully.
Despite the shallow story, I do like the actual dialogues. They're of the right length and do contain some good lines. Normally I'd skip them but for some reason I read them every time.
The jumpkick. There, I said it. I hate this attack for being the most overpowered attack in the game. You can win the entire game with it as it's powerful and impossible for your enemies to dodge. This truly ruined the experience for me and just throws the whole idea of combat realism out of the window. Sure you could refrain from executing it or download an addon for it to decrease its power but it's just not a good idea that the main game has this cheaty attack as default. This could be a really challenging game with a rewarding fighting mechanism was it not for this.
Another annoying thing that goes hand in hand with the jumpkick is that the game is really shallow in explaining the combat. The basics are there but that's about it. I suppose it comes with practise but don't tell me you're not going to give me a tutorial about the fighting system and all the things I can do. It tried to not be a button masher but really failed on this department as I tend to get lucky a lot and if not, just got to use that stupid jumpkick...
The parkouring itself isn't too bad but could use work. Often times you're asked to climb up a mountain or tower and the checkpoints are spaced out too far and the general direction is sometimes unclear or the jumps plain ridiculous and gimmicky. I wish these kind of objectives were just cutscenes instead.
Speaking of cutscenes, often times, cutscenes and interactions just get bugged with flickering, character teleportation and laggy dialogues as a result.
Now we're on the subject of bugginess, when rolling your enemies don't even seem to attack you until you stand up. They sometimes also act really odd when going for weapons to pick up.
For a 28 euro game, this is really not something I'd recommend to buy. I completed the main campaign and half of the Lugaru campaign (because at that point I was tired of the jumpkick) in about 4 hours. The campaigns are short, flawed and in the end I'm not looking back it as a thorougly enjoyable game. A shame because I really do like the concept.
For having a really long time of development since Lugaru which came out in 2005 (!), it has a lot of unpolished work lying around. This should've been early access.

This driving game has got to be the the one you never knew you wanted. It really is aptly named, you'd really feel like a truck driver. It's so weird, I never knew driving trucks would be this fun!
I play Assetto Corsa, RaceRoom Racing Experience, Project Cars, Codies F1 & DiRT, etc. Not one of them really felt close to what we normal people usually drive. Of course those games have race cars but for some reason none of them feels real when you drive at "normal everyday" speeds. In this game going 55 MPH or 60 or 70 really looks and feels like it. All other racing games and sims looks awfully slow even on 100 MPH.
This is also the first driving game I had where the automatic transmissions really feels and behaves like the real one. Maybe it's apples vs oranges but on the usual racing game and sim automatic transmissions just shift for you and most of them goes to reverse when you press the brakes while stopped. I haven't driven, read or heard of a car like that. Here on 'real automatic' mode you still have to put the gearshift to forward or reverse. And it doesn't wait for you to reach the redline before shifting up. It really felt like a real vehicle, but a super heavy one! I haven't tried the sequential and manual modes since I don't really wanna manage like 15+ forward gears.
ATS also doesn't look as pretty as, let's say, The Crew, but what it lacks in technical beauty it makes up with its immersive environments. Also it's really got road signs and rules and you have to obey them. Heck, one could use this game to learn  about US driving rules.
I wish the developers of this game would make a taxi simulator just like this.
Update: I also with the developers would optimize the graphics engine more. I have a GTX 1080 and an overclocked i5 2500K yet the FPS still drops from 60 on the cities. I know my rig isn't the latest and the greatest but it could easily run other games that look a lot more pretty at ultra settings yet never drop below 60 at 1080p. is a simplistic and fun little MOBA that has a moderate learning curve and is mostly easy to get the hang of.  It isn’t as complex or competitive as many other MOBAs out there. This is a good thing for anyone who wants to play some PVP without having to deal with an overly complicated game and an overly angry playerbase.
The game plays out in matches on small 2D arena-like maps.  At the start of each match, the players can choose from several
(read: heroes) to play as, each with their own different abilities.  Each match takes about a half hour or so, as two teams push with “creeps” to destroy towers and the enemy base. Sound familiar? So it plays like a traditional MOBA, but in 2D.
The combination of the distinctiveness of 2D MOBA combat and the well-designed abilities for the different
creates a pretty enjoyable gameplay experience. It is fun to play around with the different character combinations to see what fun you can have with the unique gameplay. Also, there is a pretty decent playerbase and the developers have consistently been updating the game and creating new content, so it appears to have a stable heartbeat.
would be a good game to consider if you are someone who is interested in playing a PVP game for fun and don’t want to deal with the hostility of the community of other MOBAs. The ranking system does its best to keep everyone around where they should win 50% of the time. But that doesn’t stop some people from believing they should be winning every single match; luckily they’re the minority in this game. Due to the simplicity of the mechanics and the lighthearted nature of the game, the community tends to be a little less unnecessarily competitive than in other games.
EDIT: As of the start of the year 2016, it has been a while since I have played this. The developers have continued to support the game with updates. I cannot speak about the current state of certain aspects of the game which may have changed since I have last played, but I believe what I have said here still holds true to the core game.

Look at this as a simulator and you'll be let down. Looking at this as a truck-themed arcade game, and you'll praise:
• An amazing map - no prefabricated undersized intersections. The bespoke highways are properly scaled and a joy to drive on. You can do more than 30mph without tipping over. The map itself is huge - takes several hours to cross despite higher speeds and straighter roads than ETS
• You can see your hired drivers on the road as they work, and join them in competitive jobs
• A far, far, far more detailed truck diagnostics system than other games. Worn brake pads grind against the discs and degrade braking performance. Panels get beat up, the engine runs like crap.
• The truck upgrade system is excellent and features things like side and rear mounted cameras to cover blind spots.
• Cops (could be a con for some!)
• Nice side-missions, help out hitchhikers if you want, pick up extra jobs from cafés or over the radio
That isn't to say this game is without flaws. The iffy handling and dodgy physics are geared to racing, not driving. There are competitive jobs where you are pitted against other drivers to race cargo to its destination (very unrealistic). There are also truck races and out-of-this-world missions to complete, too.
In summary, don't look at it as a sim and you will be able to forgive its shortcomings. Go for a race or forgive the iffy handling and go for a really scenic drive.

I love Pendulo games so I had high hopes for this. I love their classic point and click games, they have some flaws like some illogical puzzles, but most of the time their games are good and I enjoy them. I especially like their stories. This game is far from perfect but I enjoyed it.
I wish they would’ve stick to old classic formula of the genre. Broken sword 5 got back to the roots and it shines, it has that nostalgia feeling, looks and plays great. For some reason Pendulo gone 3D. Yeah I get it Pendulo you have 3D designers who  can design 3D items and you can view and rotate them. But why waste resources on this? “oh look a hammer in 3D”, every inexperienced 3D artist can do this. Instead you could’ve paid more attention to actual gameplay. It feels like all the work was done for making all those characters and items and the ability to rotate and  view them from all the sides. Oh and when you give the item to another character there is a slow close up animation. You can look at other characters and inspect them like in Sherlock Holmes games or Agatha Christie ABC murders, only it doesn’t make much sense here. Pointless. Wasted resources. And what’s wrong with combining items? Let’s say there’s item A and item B and they must be combined. You look at item A and then try to use item B and it doesn’t work. To make it work you must first look at item B and then use item A on it. What the ♥♥♥♥? It’s not that way with all the items, but I was stuck because of this.
Hotspots sometimes doesn’t work. You may be close to it but if you’re too close you can’t click on it or if you’re at slightly wrong angle you can’t click it either. You must be at the correct angle and distance to click on a hotspot. Why?!
Sound is strange in this game. Music starts playing and ends abruptly, then only silence. What’s the logic behind this? I don’t want to play in silence, I like having some background music playing.
Voice acting is passable, I expected better, especially for this price, at times it’s just horrible. Graphics are pretty nice. Environments are very good, it’s nice to look at it. Characters could use some work though, they often look emotionless. But i prefer 2D characters anyway.
The price is another thing this game fails. It’s an adventure game, a niche genre with no replayability, people are not going to pay 30€ for it, I guess at least 5€ was added to the price because of denuvo. Aaaaand it got cracked. Nicely done. Steamspy says it sold less than 10 000 copies, I think that’s pretty bad.
I still hope Pendulo will make another game, but next time please go back to the classic point and click formula.
I Don’t know how to rate this game, I’d give a neutral rating but I can’t do that here. So in hope that Pendulo can make a better game I’m giving this a thumbs up. It’s worth playing if you’re an adventure fan and enjoy a good dark story, but it’s nothing specia. Wait for a sale.

And I had idly poised my pen in air
To stop it with a period of ink
When something strange about it made me think,
This was no dust speck by my breathing blown,
But unmistakably a living mite
With inclinations it could call its own.
It paused as with suspicion of my pen,
And then came racing wildly on again
To where my manuscript was not yet dry;
Then paused again and either drank or smelt--
With loathing, for again it turned to fly.
Plainly with an intelligence I dealt.
It seemed too tiny to have room for feet,
Yet must have had a set of them complete
To express how much it didn't want to die.
It ran with terror and with cunning crept.
It faltered: I could see it hesitate;
Then in the middle of the open sheet
Cower down in desperation to accept
Whatever I accorded it of fate.
I have none of the tenderer-than-thou
Collectivistic regimenting love
With which the modern world is being swept.
But this poor microscopic item now!
Since it was nothing I knew evil of
I let it lie there till I hope it slept.
I have a mind myself and recognize
Mind when I meet with it in any guise
No one can know how glad I am to find
On any sheet the least display of mind.

This is an absolute treat of a point and click adventure. I'd suggest playing the first Yesterday game before this but there is just about enough explanation for this game to stand alone. Note that even though it's labelled 'Origins' it's more of a sequel than a prequel. Half the plot takes place after the events of the original Yesterday game and the rest is a collection of flashbacks/memories.
Best things:
Puzzle mechanic- the puzzles are of the 'use inventory object with something in your surroundings type' but often requiring you to justify your action by referring back to something else you did or heard. For example, trying to 'throw pebble at window'' will prompt you to refer back to a conversation where you learned you needed to create a distraction. That's a crude example but hopefully you get the idea.
Plot and script:  intriguing throughout, a great mystery story.  It's very dark in places but has retained a subtle yet twisted sense of humour.
Value for money - it's got a good length of play. Maybe 20 hours assuming no walkthrough.
Production - good graphics, decent although not exceptional soundtrack. No bugs that I can recall.
Worst things:
honestly, there's not much to criticise. A couple of the voice actors aren't great. A few minor elements of the plot get a bit too far fetched. The penultimate chapter seemed to distract from the pace of the main plot. These criticisms are very, very much nit-picking.
In short: thoroughly recommended if you like a good story and like games that really make you think.
Minor caveat: if you own a wine set you might find you can't look at it in the same way ever again. ;)

I'm honestly astounded this game is Mostly Negative for recent reviews. I just came to the game after wondering what happened to it after launch. I'm VERY impressed. This is one of the best survival and crafting games I've played in the last few years. Much better than my short time in RUST before I refunded it due to the toxic players.
I have played Single Player/PvE and it's been a blast. I'm around 20 hours in and still loving it. There's a few bugs and, aside from one infuriating one that's making my captured people disappear, rendering the thrall system useless, the bugs have not been too bad for me. Performance on my 1070 has been decent. Not the best in places, but rarely slideshow quality. I do really wish they would increase view distance for NPCs though, I've been attacked by pop-in hyenas a number of times.
The new content they have added looks amazing. I watched a 10 hour live stream of Strippin and Dodger play to get there. I really enjoy the fact that they are putting in dedicated PvE content like dungeons. Overall, it seems like this is the most PvE friendly survival game yet. The AI problems I've heard others speak about don't seem that big of a deal to me. Sure you can cheese them with rocks, but to a certain degree that's required since they will wreck your day if you get attacked by more than 1-2. And there's enough bowmen to make that strategy not the greatest anyway.
Overall, I fully recommend this game if you have a mid-high grade system, and are primarily interested in Single player or group PvE. I have not played MP yet, but I hope to get a friend or two who want to play and start over. The map is big enough that living in a different zone would basically be a different experience.
I guess you can keep moving if you only like PvP in your survival games. If that's the case, I somewhat wonder why you are looking at Conan anyway since Rust and Ark serve your niche so well already, and most/all other smaller Survival games seem to lean towards PvP too, aside from The Long Dark.
Anyway, PvP players, feel free to stay away, PvE fans are welcome.

Honestly i've played alot of this game and there is a few things I must list off.
1. Insanely good graphics- This is a good thing for me and alot of other users/players out there with bad computers.
Even though my computer is bad I can run this on its highest graphics which is a good thing for me.
2. Fast Paced Combat- Alot of you know what that is but unlike other mmorpgs this is a hard thing to do but fun.
It makes you analyze your opponents and choose what skills you use, but thats not this same for all classes some class you can just get in there kill and walk out ( of course looting the dead npcs enemys first ).
3. Friendly community- This is said to be in alot of mmorpgs but thanks to the mods and admins everyone here is nice, funny, and you can always find someone to help you with a harder dungeon. Which leads me to my next one.
4. Dungeons- The dungeons may get a little repetitive but thats just with the design and even thats not guaranteed. With each new level there's different groups of enemys, places, chests, bosses. The only way I found so far to get the same exact level is to play the same one again.
5. Fun Story Line- This may not seem like a big one but it is, without a fun story line the game's just not worth playing.
This game has a interesting story line to say the least, not only that, but it keeps you on you feet. Even when I got bored and left the game to do something else, I always kept coming back to see what happens next.
6. Completely Free- This game is completely free which is hard to say since I gave it good reviews and it's free, but it's true. You can do everything in the story line even the expansions. This is the one exception, and that's the market place which is to be expected in any MMO/RPG or combination of the two.
So all in all this is a really great game.

Audio - I think the explosions and soundtrack is very intense, especially in ranked. I think they need to add some other audio tracks instead of having the exact same one every level i play. It does get annoying quite a lot so. I rate Audio 7/10.
Gameplay - There are 4 game modes and over 10 different game add-ons (i.e Lethal Spikes). Practice, Casual, Ranked and Story. The goal of each level is to outrun your competitors and outrun them out of the screen. Once they are off screen, they are dead. There are also power ups which could be like; missiles, grappling hook, fireball, freeze ray, drill etc. These make the game intense but for every single powerup, there is a way to dodge it. For example, if there is a grappling hook coming out of nowhere, all you have to do is press the slide key and you can dodge it. There are many obstacles like blocks which you have to slide under, spikes that if you land on them you are stunned and more. Finally, we have game add-ons. These can be acquired by levelling up. This means while ingame (practice or online), the host can put these on. For example, ‘Lethal spikes’ means that if you land on the spike, you die.
Characters - There is not much to say here. While levelling up, you also unlock new characters and skins. When you start, you are given the default 4 characters. Comrade, Unic, Hothead and Speedrunner. While levelling up, you also get characters like Neko. There is one thing i found out recently. If you do a command like ‘/gangbeast’ or ‘/wolf’ you get characters from different games. /gangbeast gives you all the colour gang beasts from the silly physics game. ‘/wolf’ ‘/dallas’ ‘/houston’ and more give you the famous characters from the Payday series.
Trails - There is hardly anything to say. When you start off, you get the normal boring trail which is your character moving fast. BUT, If you go to the trail store or community store, you can buy trails like i have and others like ‘Angel’ and ‘Spectrum’ and ‘Unic’. In the store, they range from £0.79 / $1 but in the community hub, they range from £0.49 / $0.70 - £1.49 / $2. These are recommended if you want to look like a famous player.
Graphics / Visuals - The visuals are really nice and smooth. They have no pixels and look very well designed.

THIS GAME IS AWESOME.
That was the short version, now I'll try to say a bit more. As a point'n'click lover, I played many of them, but YO is one of the very few who made say "wow, that's brilliant".
The story itself is very good, the characters are interesting, and the devs were clever enough to use original mechanics in a genre which lacks it. While common point'n'clicks will use a standard inventory, with objects you can combine with other objects or environment items, YO is also adding other things. You have an inventory for objects, but also another one for informations / ideas. This gives the opportunity to go deeper with combinations. There's also another nice thing: the multi-combination. 5th screenshot starting from the right on the store page shows what it means. In my humble opinion it really makes things more interesting.
There are also different times involved in the game, making player feel totally different atmospheres. And some comments from the game, when trying weird combinations, are really hilarious. It's not for a small child and for people who don't like to laugh with dark things. I highly recommend the game to everyone else :)

It's addicting to play, I like the whole idea of building things to use in the game.  I'm going to list the Cons first:
Cons:
-Graphics are pretty basic, but the game it free
-There are about a billion quests and you can only have so many on the active page so you can spend a lot of time wandering around doing quests and not realize you had two others you could have done while you were there.  Now you have to go back where you just were to do those.
-If you follow along the recommended quest lines, and skip the others in order to level up, you will be in over your head quickly.  Not to mention some of the quest lines are 25 minute rides on a horse between them.
-This can be a good thing or a bad thing, stands out bad to me, but respawns of enemies/creatures is WAY too fast.  I understand that if there are a lot of people playing the same area with the same quests, you need to have respawns set faster in order for people not waiting so much, but this game has been out for a while and it's very rare to be questing near anyone else.  If you are involved in clearing an area out and meet the boss, you retreat a little to reload/heal whatever and you will run into all the people you just killed and die in a horde.  They really need to make some of the bigger quest jobs into their own instance without enemy/creature respawn.  The game uses instances for some quests, they just need to do it more often, like the PRISON!!
Pros:
-I find people are very helpful in help chat.  I have seen the same question come up in less than 10 minutes from three different people and someone is willing to answer it all three times without being a smartass.
-Lots of higher level players give things out to lower levels players which helps a lot in the leveling process.  I got 50R from someone early in the game and can buy anything I want now at my level and I have a ton left over.  Thanks dude!
-It's fun gameplay,
As a final note, you can do surveys on the Fallen Earth website (not really, they redirect you to a company that handles it).  These surveys can drive you insane.  You can choose to do a 15 minute survey for a certain amount of points and then do 10 minutes of a "pre" survey to determine that you are not a match for the "real" survey and receive nothing.  That needs to be fixed.  I think when I initially started doing surveys for points, I spent two hours doing them, selected about 15 different surveys and only received credit for doing two.  Not worth my time.  You should at least get something for doing the "pre" surveys even if you arent a match for the real one.
Anyways, fun game, kinda basic, surveys can be PITA.

I only write reviews for some of my favorite games on Steam... and this one qualifies. I love the customization, everyone will customize their vehicle to their liking, and very rarely have I seen two of the same vehicle. However, some thing's dont seem right. For example, I built a spider-tank with 225 HP and a large cannon on the front which was supposed to do 60 damage per direct hit. Sounds pretty powerful right? Well, you would be wrong, as a starter vehicle was able to destroy me. Why? He got the jump on me. Literally the only reason. Think of that what you will. Another problem I had with this is the pricing of items in the game, as well as the storage mechanic. In order to build vehicles in the game, you are required to buy items using a currency called "G". What is the problem of this? Items cost up to 15 "G" in game, and you will only get 3 "G" per game, unless of course you manage to destroy 10 other vehicles, which will earn you one more "G".Then there is the storage mechanic. In the beginning of the game you will only have storage for 6 parts. But you only get storage for 1 more part whenever you level up. Not to mention the fact that, even if you spent 15 "G" on a part you will only get 1 "G" for selling it. Which makes it a problem to try and store lots of items.
But despite these flaws, I keep playing it. The game is fun to play, and in the end, Isn't that what matters? Also when it says free, they actually mean free.

At current full price, unless you are rich I’d recommend waiting for a very good sale*. edit - They have removed a lot of the extra empty hotspots, and improved mouse control to a normal point and click game, both very welcome changes and will save you a lot of time with those hotspot achievements!
GENERAL
Gameplay there is a lot of Sherlock Holmes type of observation of others, finding main hotspots (which there is a hotspot helper) there was no big puzzles and is very linear in areas to explore.  It’s a good game for people new to adventure games.

The time spent anywhere else but in events, on battlefields or the world map is neglectable and these three playgrounds are all extremely similar every time.
On top of this, and this to me is the greatest flaw about the game, Overfall tries to appear casual and intimately atmospheric at the same time, with one perspective destroying the other. The art style to me is too cartoony, the writing includes too much light-hearted banter. It just falls flat on delivering a consistent experience.
I do recommend the game to genre enthusiasts but be aware that depending on your expectations in terms of immersion and

This game has a ways to go, but development is still very active and I like where it's going so it gets a thumb up from me. This is my preferred genre, the survival crafting games, and I only play them single player. So this review doesn't cover the multiplayer aspect of the game. My other favorite is Empyrion.
Often these types of games can feel empty for the single player if there isn't much to do, but Conan delivers in this area where other survival crafting games have more to offer for the multiplayer community. Exploring through caves/dungeons, raiding enemy encampments, and searching out/crafting rare items adds a lot of stuff to do along with the crafting and building. The types of buildings you can create are nice also because you can build them off the side of cliffs which adds to the possibilities.
There are of course still bugs, but this is EA so it's to be expected. At the time of writing this the game was on sale for $19.99, so I would consider that a fair price, but I think I would leave it for now if it weren't on sale. These EA titles really need to consider their price tags given the state they can be in. If you're reluctant to purchase now it's understandable given some of the other reviews. But I would at least keep my eye on this one. Of all the EA titles that have 'potential' out there, this one is looking to be one of my favorites once they get it more stable and polished.
